x: God Almighty means by His saying: O Prophet,
divorce them during their waiting period

. He says: If you divorce your women, divorce them during their period of purity, which they count from their waiting period, pure from without intercourse, and do not divorce them during their menstruation, which they do not count from their menstrual cycles. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said:
m: I heard Al-A’mash, on the authority of Malik bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: Divorce is for the waiting period while she is pure and has not had intercourse.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Malik ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: h
Divorce them during their waiting period
. He said: During the period of purity without intercourse.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: If you divorce women,
h
divorce them during their waiting period
. He said: If you divorce, he said: Purity without intercourse.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: h
Divorce them during their waiting period
. He said: Purity from without intercourse.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Dawud bin Husayn, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that he used to consider divorce according to the Sunnah to be permissible when a woman is pure from intercourse, and during every period of purity, which is the waiting period that God has commanded.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of ʿAbdullah bin Abi Najeh, on the authority of Humayd Al-Aʿraj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: that a man asked Ibn Abbas and said: He divorced his wife one hundred times. He said: You disobeyed your Lord, and your wife left you, and you did not fear God, so He would make a way out for you. And he recited this verse: And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out. And he said: O Prophet,
h
when you divorce women
h
divorce them during their waiting period

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Samad Ibn Abd Al-Warith told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Hamid Al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us:
m: Ayoub Surat Divorce: 1 O Prophet,
h
when you divorce women
, divorce them for their prescribed waiting period and keep count of the waiting period and fear God, your Lord.
h
Do not turn them out of their houses

, nor should they leave [their homes] unless they commit a clear immorality. These are the limits of God. And whoever transgresses the limits of God has certainly wronged himself. You do not know; perhaps God will cause [something] to happen. After that, something told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Kathir, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: I was with Ibn Abbas when a man came to him and said: He divorced his wife three times. He remained silent until we thought that he had taken her back. Then he said: One of you would go and commit a foolish act, then say: O Ibn Abbas, O Ibn Abbas, and God, the Almighty, said: And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out. But if you do not fear God, then I find no way out for you. You have disobeyed your Lord, and your wife has become separated from you. God, the Almighty, said: O Prophet,
h
when you divorce women
h
divorce them during their waiting period

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, who said:
m: I heard Mujahid narrating a hadith on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: O Prophet,
h
when you divorce women
h
divorce them during their waiting period
. Ibn Abbas said: Before their waiting period.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Umayya, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: that he recited:
h
Divorce them during their waiting period

c: Al-Abbas bin Abdul-Azim told us: Jaafar bin Awn told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
So divorce them during their waiting period
. He said: Pure except for intercourse.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Harun bin Al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Muslim, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then divorce them during their waiting period

, he said: Pure and not menstruating, or pregnant and her pregnancy has become evident. He said: Harun narrated to us, on the authority of Isa bin Yazid bin Daab, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, regarding the one who wanted to pronounce three divorces all at once, that there is nothing wrong with him as long as he divorces her before her waiting period, as God commanded him, and they disliked for a man to divorce his wife with one divorce, or two divorces, or three divorces, if it was not during the waiting period that God mentioned.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Awn told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin that he said:
m: Concerning His statement,
h
Then divorce them during their waiting period
, he said: He divorces her while she is pure, without intercourse, or a pregnancy that is evident.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty,
h
So divorce them during their waiting period
, he said: during their purification.

c: Ali bin Abdul A’la Al-Maharbi told us: Al-Maharbi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding the statement of God, O Prophet,
h
when you divorce women

, divorce them for their waiting period, he said: The waiting period is the menstrual period, and the menstrual period is the period of menstruation, and the pure woman is the woman who is pure without intercourse, then she experiences three menstrual periods.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, O Prophet,
h
when you divorce women
, divorce them for their waiting period. The waiting period is that he divorces her while she is pure and has not had intercourse with her, with a single divorce.

c: Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
Divorce them during their waiting period

, he said: If she becomes pure from menstruation without intercourse. I said: How? He said: If she becomes pure before you touch her, then if you wish to divorce her again, leave her until she menstruates another time, then divorce her when she becomes pure the second time. If you want to divorce her a third time, wait until she menstruates, and when she becomes pure, divorce her a third time. Then she observes one waiting period, then she may marry again if she wishes. He said: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Ibn Tawus said: If you want to divorce her, divorce her once when she is pure before you touch her, and you should not do more than that until three menstrual periods have passed, because one divorce separates her.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
Then divorce them during their waiting period
, that he said: He divorced her while she was pure and without intercourse.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
So divorce them during their waiting period

, he said: If you divorce her during the waiting period, then her ownership is in your hand. Whoever divorces during the waiting period, God gives him latitude in that regard, and gives him ownership if he wants to take her back before the waiting period ends, he can take her back.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us: Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
When you divorce women
h
divorce them during their waiting period
, he said: While she is pure and has not had intercourse. If she does not menstruate, then at the beginning of each new moon.

c: Abu al-Sa’ib told me: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Ubayd God, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said:
m: I divorced my wife while she was menstruating. Umar came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform him. He said: Order him to take her back until she is pure, then menstruates, then purifies herself, then if he wishes he may divorce her before having intercourse with her, and if he wishes he may keep her, for it is the waiting period that God Almighty said: He said:

c: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: in a similar manner, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: that he divorced his wife while she was menstruating. Umar asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Tell him to take her back, then to keep her until she is pure, then menstruates, then becomes pure, then if he wants he may keep her. That is the waiting period during which God has commanded women to be divorced.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: that he divorced his wife while she was menstruating. Umar came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him. He ordered him to take her back and then leave her until she became pure and then menstruated, then he could divorce her. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is the waiting period for which God has commanded that women be divorced, meaning until they become pure.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Divorce them during their waiting period

, he said: He should not divorce her while she is menstruating, nor during a period of purity that he has set for her, but rather he should leave her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then he should divorce her once. If she menstruates, then her waiting period is three menstrual periods, and if she does not menstruate, then her waiting period is three months, and if she is pregnant, then her waiting period is until she gives birth.

c: Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Saʿid ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz,
m: who was asked about the words of God,
h
Divorce them during their waiting period

. He said: The Sunnah divorce is for a man to divorce his wife once while she is in her waiting period and is pure from not having had intercourse with her, then he leaves her. If he wishes, he may take her back before she has washed herself after the third menstrual period. If he wants to divorce her three times, he should divorce her once while she is in her waiting period and is pure from not having had intercourse with her, then he should leave her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then he should divorce her again, then he should leave her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then he should divorce her again, then she is not permissible for him until she marries another husband. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a reason for his divorce of Hafsa.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divorced Hafsa bint Umar once, and this verse was revealed: O Prophet,
h
when you divorce women

, divorce them for their prescribed waiting period. It was said: Take her back, for she is a woman who fasts and prays, and she is one of your women in Paradise. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement, And count the number, he said: Keep track of the number. And His statement: And fear God, your Lord, and
h
do not turn them out of their houses

. He says: And fear God, O people, your Lord, and beware of transgressing His limits. Do not turn out those of your women whom you have divorced during their waiting period from the houses in which you had housed them before the divorce until their waiting period has expired. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his statement, And fear God, your Lord, and
h
do not turn them out of their homes
until their waiting period is over.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Ibn Jurayj told us: Ata’ said:
m: If he gives her permission to observe her waiting period somewhere other than his house, and she observes her waiting period in her family’s house, then he has shared in the sin with her. Then he recited: And
h
do not turn them out of their houses
, nor should they leave unless they commit a clear immorality. He said: I said: Is this verse about this one? He said: Yes.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Haywah ibn Shuraih told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ajlan, on the authority of Nafi’,
m: that Abdullah ibn Umar used to say about this verse:
h
Do not turn them out of their houses

, nor should they leave unless they commit a clear immorality. He said: Her leaving before the expiration of the waiting period. Ibn Ajlan said, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam: If Surat Divorce: 1 O Prophet,
h
when you divorce women
, divorce them for their prescribed waiting period and keep count of the waiting period and fear God, your Lord.
h
Do not turn them out of their houses

, nor should they leave [their homes] unless they commit a clear immorality. These are the limits of God. And whoever transgresses the limits of God has certainly wronged himself. You do not know; perhaps God will cause [something] to happen. After that, something she commits an immorality, she is to be turned out.

c: Ali bin Abdul A’la Al-Maharbi told us: Al-Maharbi told us
m: Abdul Rahman bin Muhammad, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement,
h
Do not turn them out of their houses

, nor should they leave unless they commit a clear immorality, he said: She is not to go out except with his permission, and the husband is not to turn her out while she is in her waiting period. If she goes out, then she has no place to live or to receive maintenance.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, “And fear God, your Lord.
h
Do not turn them out of their houses
, nor should they leave them.” He said: She is the divorced woman who does not leave her house, as long as her husband has the right to take her back, and she is in her waiting period.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Do not turn them out of their homes
, nor should they leave. This is if he divorces her once or twice, she has the right to do so unless he divorces her three times. His saying,
h
And they should not go out unless they commit a clear immorality
. God Almighty says: Do not send them out unless they commit a clear immorality that is clear to anyone who witnesses it or knows about it.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the immorality mentioned in this passage, and the meaning for which God permitted them to be expelled from their homes while they were in their waiting period.
Some of them said: The immorality mentioned by God in this passage is adultery, and the expulsion that God permitted is expulsion to carry out the prescribed punishment.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Do not turn them out of their homes
, nor should they leave unless they commit a clear immorality, he said: Adultery. He said: So she goes out so that the punishment can be carried out on her.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: the same.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told us: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Salih ibn Muslim, who said:
m: I asked Aamer: If a man divorces his wife once, should he expel her from her home? He said: If she is an adulteress.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Do not turn them out of their homes
, nor should they leave unless they commit a clear immorality, he said: Unless they commit adultery.

c: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, and I asked him about the statement of God, the Almighty: And
h
do not turn them out of their houses
, nor should they leave unless they commit a clear immorality. He said: God, the Most High, said, And those of your women who commit immorality
r
(An-Nisa’: 15)
. He said: These are the chaste women. Then bring to witness against them four witnesses from among you
r
(An-Nisa’: 15)

... the verse. He said: So God made their way stoning, so she should not leave her house unless she commits a clear immorality. So if she commits a clear immorality, she should be taken out to the prescribed punishment and stoned. Before this, the chaste woman was to be confined in her house and not allowed to marry, and the virgins were to be harmed. God, the Most High, said, And those of you who commit it, punish them both
r
(An-Nisa’: 16)
. O adulterer, O adulteress. “But if they repent and amend, then turn away from them. Indeed, God is ever Accepting of repentance and Merciful.”
r
(An-Nisa’: 16)
:16] He said: Then he abrogated all of this, and made stoning for the married man and woman, and made one hundred lashes for the unmarried men. He said: And this was abrogated.

x: Others said: The obscenity that God meant in this place is: obscenity towards one’s in-laws.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: God said:
h
Do not turn them out of their homes
, nor should they leave unless they commit a clear immorality. He said: A clear immorality is that she commits a sin against her family.

x: Others said: Rather, it is every disobedience to God.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Unless they commit a clear immorality. Immorality is a sin.

x: Others said: Rather, it is her rebellion against her husband, so he divorces her for her rebellion, and she is then entitled to move from her home.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Unless they commit a clear immorality. Qatada said: Unless he divorces her for disobedience, then she has the right to move from her husband’s house.

x: Others said: The clear indecency that God Almighty mentioned in this place is her leaving her home.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us: Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And they should not leave unless they commit a clear immorality
, he said: Her leaving her house is an immorality.

x: Some of them said that her leaving if she commits an immorality means that she should leave and the prescribed punishment should be carried out on her.

c: Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me: Saʿid ibn al-Hakam ibn Abi Maryam told us: Yahya ibn Ayoub told us: Muhammad ibn ʿAjlan told us, on the authority of Nafiʿ, on the authority of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Do not turn them out of their houses

, nor should they leave unless they commit a clear immorality, he said: Her leaving before the end of the waiting period is an immorality. The correct statement in my opinion is the statement of those who said: What is meant by immorality in this context is disobedience. This is because immorality is every ugly thing in which the limit is exceeded. Fornication is among these, as are theft and obscenity towards in-laws, and her leaving her home in which she is required to observe her waiting period. So whatever she does while she is in her waiting period, her husband has the right to expel her from that home, for committing the immorality that she committed. And His statement,
h
And these are the limits set by God

, means that God, the Exalted, says: These matters that I have explained to you, such as divorce during the waiting period, counting the waiting period, the command to fear God, and that the divorced woman not leave her home unless she commits a clear immorality, are the limits set by God for you, O people, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of God has wronged himself, means that God, the Exalted, says: And whoever transgresses the limits set by God for His creation has wronged himself, meaning: he has earned a burden for himself, and thus he has become unjust to himself and transgressed against himself. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ali bin Abdul A’la told us: Abdul Rahman bin Muhammad Al-Maharbi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
And these are the limits set by God
, he said: This is obedience to God, so do not transgress them. He said: He says: Whoever does anything other than this has wronged himself. And His saying: You do not know,
h
perhaps God will bring about something new after

that. God Almighty says: You do not know what will happen, perhaps God will bring about a return after your divorce of them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri,
m: that Fatimah bint Qais was married to Abu Hafs al-Makhzumi, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had appointed Ali as governor of some part of Yemen. He went out with him and sent her a divorce that she had received, and he ordered Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah al-Makhzumi and al-Harith ibn Hisham to provide for her. They said: No, by God, we do not provide for her unless she is pregnant. So she came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him, but he did not provide for her unless she was pregnant. She asked his permission to move, and she said: Where should I move, O Messenger of God? He said: With Ibn Umm Kulthum, who was blind. She would put her clothes down with him, but he could not see her. She remained there until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her to Usama ibn Zayd when her waiting period had passed. Marwan ibn al-Hakam sent to her asking her about this hadith, so she told him. Marwan said: We have not heard this hadith except from a woman, and we will adhere to the protection that we found people upon. Fatima said: There is a book between me and you. God Almighty said:
h
So divorce them during their waiting period
until He reached:
h
Perhaps God will bring about after that something new
. She said: What new thing will happen after the three? It is only about a man taking back his wife. How can a woman be kept without maintenance?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Perhaps God will bring about something new after
that, meaning this is regarding a man returning to his wife.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: You do not know,
h
perhaps God will bring about something new after
that: meaning, a revision.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: You do not know,
h
perhaps God will bring about something new after
that. He said: He will return to her in this house of hers once or twice, which is further from adultery. Saeed said, and Al-Hasan said: This is in one and two, and what God brings about after three.

c: Yaqub told us, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ayoub told us, he said:
m: I heard Al-Hasan and Ikrimah say: The woman who has been divorced three times and whose husband has died has no right to housing or maintenance. He said: Ikrimah said, Perhaps God will bring about something after that. He said: What happens after the three divorces?

c: Ali bin Abdul-A’la Al-Maharbi told us: Abdul-Rahman bin Muhammad Al-Maharbi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Perhaps God will bring about something Surat Divorce
: 1 O Prophet,
h
when you divorce women
, divorce them for their prescribed waiting period and keep count of the waiting period and fear God, your Lord.
h
Do not turn them out of their houses

, nor should they leave [their homes] unless they commit a clear immorality. These are the limits of God. And whoever transgresses the limits of God has certainly wronged himself. You do not know; perhaps God will cause [something] to happen. After that, something new after that, he said: Perhaps the man will take her back during her waiting period.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, You do not know,
h
perhaps God will bring about something new after
that, that he had no right to return to her.

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: You do not know,
h
perhaps God will bring about something new after
that. He said: The return.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Perhaps God will bring about after that something new

, he said: Perhaps God will bring about in your heart that you will take your wife back. He said: He said: And whoever divorces during the waiting period, God has given him latitude in that regard, and has given him the right to take her back if he wants to take her back before the waiting period ends, he can take her back.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan:
m: Perhaps God will bring about something after that. He said: Perhaps he will return to her.

evidence.text: And he recited this verse: And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out.

x: And when they have reached their term

, God Almighty says: When the divorced women who are in their waiting period have reached their term, that is when their number is about to expire, then keep them according to acceptable terms, meaning: So keep them by taking them back, if you want that according to acceptable terms, meaning: with what God has commanded you to keep, which is by giving her the rights that God has made obligatory upon him of maintenance, clothing, housing, and good companionship, or separate from them according to acceptable terms, or leave them when their number has expired, then she will be separated from you according to acceptable terms, meaning by giving her what she has a right over him of the dowry and compensation according to what he has made obligatory upon her. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ali ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Al-Maharibi Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad told me, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And when they have reached their term

, meaning: If her waiting period has ended before she has washed herself after the third menstrual period, or three months if she has not menstruated, he said: Then take her back if you want to take her back before the waiting period ends by keeping her in an acceptable manner, and what is acceptable is to treat her well, or release her with kindness. Release with kindness means that he leaves her until her waiting period has ended and gives her a dowry if he owes her a dowry if he has to divorce her, so that is release with kindness, and the compensation is according to what is possible.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And when they have reached their term
, he said: If he divorces her once or twice, he wants to keep her on acceptable terms, or release her with kindness. His saying,
h
And bring to witness two just men among you

, and bring to witness the retention if you retain them, and that is the return, two just men among you, and they are the two whose religion and trustworthiness are acceptable. We have previously explained justice in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here, and we mentioned what the scholars said about it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: If he wants to take her back before her waiting period is over, he should have two witnesses, as God said,
h
And bring to witness two just men among you

at the time of divorce and at the time of taking her back. If he takes her back, she is with him on two divorces. If Surat al-Talaq 65:2 So when they have reached their term, either keep them according to acceptable terms or part with them according to acceptable terms. And bring to witness two just men from among you
h
and establish the testimony for God
. This is an admonition to whoever believes in God and the Last Day.
h
And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out

. he does not take her back, then when her waiting period is over, she is separated from him with one divorce, and she has control over herself. Then she can marry whomever she wants, him or someone else.

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us
m: regarding his statement,
h
And bring to witness two just men among you
, he said: Regarding divorce and taking back a wife. His statement,
h
And establish the testimony for God

, means: And bear witness to the truth if you are called upon to bear witness, and give it in truth if you are called upon to give it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And establish the testimony for God
, he said: Bear witness to the truth. And His statement,
h
This is an admonition to him who believes in God and the Last Day

, God Almighty says: This that I have commanded you with, and made known to you regarding the matter of divorce, and what is due to some of you over others when separating and keeping, is an admonition from us to you, with which we admonish whoever believes in God and the Last Day, and who believes in it. What I mean by the saying whoever believes in God is whoever has faith in God.

c: Like what Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, he said: believes in Him. And His statement:
h
And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out

. God the Most High says: Whoever fears God and does what He has commanded him to do and avoids what He has forbidden, He will make a way out for him in his matter, by making him know that what He has decreed must come to pass. This is because if the divorcer divorces, as God has urged him to do for the waiting period, and does not take her back during her waiting period until it has ended and then his soul pursues it, God will make a way out for him in what his soul pursues, by making a way for him to propose to her and marry her. If he divorces her three times, he will not have that way.

x: And He provides for him from where he does not expect

, means: And He causes for him the means of provision from where he does not feel or know. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that, and some of them mentioned that this verse was revealed because of Awf bin Malik Al-Ashja’i.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Salt told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out
, he said: He knows that it is from God, and that God is the One who gives and withholds.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq:
m: h
And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out

. He said: The way out is to know that if God, the Blessed and Exalted, will give him, and if He wills, He will withhold from him. And will provide for him from where he does not expect. He said: From where he does not know.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq,
m: similarly.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out
, meaning his salvation from every distress in this world and the Hereafter, and will provide for him from where he does not expect.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn al-Mundhir, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim:
m: h
And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out
. He said: From everything that is difficult for people.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out
. He said: Whoever divorces as God has commanded him, He will make for him a way out.

c: Ali bin Abdul A’la Al-Maharbi told me: Abdul Rahman bin Muhammad Al-Maharbi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out
, and
h
And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out

. He said: What is meant by the way out and ease is if he divorces once and then remains silent about it, then if he wishes he may take her back with the testimony of two just men. This is the ease that God said. But if her waiting period has passed and he has not taken her back, then he is a suitor among those who propose, and this is what God has commanded. This is how divorce is done according to the Sunnah. As for the one who divorces at every menstrual period, he has erred in accordance with the Sunnah, disobeyed the Lord, and has encountered hardship.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out

, he said: It is applied according to the Sunnah, and it is referred to according to the Sunnah. He claimed that a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was called Awf Al-Ashja’i, and he had a son, and the polytheists had taken him prisoner, so he was among them. His father would come and complain to him about the place of his son, the condition he was in and his need, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would order him to be patient and say to him: God will make a way out for him. Shortly after that, his son escaped from the hands of the enemy, and he passed by some of the enemy’s sheep, so he drove them away and brought them to his father, and he brought with him some wealth that he had acquired from the sheep, so this verse was revealed:
h
And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out

* And will provide for him from where he does not expect. Ibn Humayd narrated: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ammar ibn Abi Muawiyah Ad-Dahni, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi Al-Jaʿd:
h
And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out

. He said: It was revealed about a man from the Ashjaʿ tribe who came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was exhausted. He asked him a question, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Fear God and be patient. He said: I have done so. So he went to his people and they said: What did he say to you? He said: “He said: ‘Fear God and be patient.’ I said: “I have done so,” until he said that three times. Then he returned and found his son, who had been a prisoner among the Banu so-and-so of the Arabs, and he had brought goats with him. He returned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Surat al-Talaq 65:3
h
And He provides for him from where he does not expect
h
And whoever relies upon God - then He is sufficient for him

. Indeed, God will accomplish His purpose. God has already set for everything a [decreed] extent. said: “My son was a prisoner among the Banu so-and-so, and he has brought goats. Are they permissible for us?” He said: Yes. He said: “Hakam told us, he said:

c: Amr told us, on the authority of Ammar Al-Dahni, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Jaʿd,
m: regarding His statement, ‘
h
And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out

.’ He said: It was revealed about a man from the Ashjaʿ tribe who was afflicted with hardship, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to him: Fear God and be patient. So he returned and found his son who had been a prisoner, and God had freed him from their hands, and he had captured some goats. So he came and mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Will you permit me, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes.” He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn al-Mundhir al-Thawri, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim, He makes a way out for him. He said: From everything that is difficult for people. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, He makes a way out for him. He said: He knows that if God wills, He will prevent him, and if He wills, He will give him.
h
And He provides for him from where he does not expect

. He said: From where he does not know. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Aruba, on the authority of Qatada, He will make a way out for him, he said: from the doubts of matters, and the distress at death, and will provide for him from where he does not expect, from where he does not hope or expect.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And He provides for him from where he does not expect
, he does not hope or expect. And His statement,
h
And whoever relies upon God - then He is sufficient for him
, God Almighty says: And whoever fears God in his affairs and entrusts them to Him - then He is sufficient for him. His saying, Indeed, God will accomplish His purpose is separate from his saying,
h
And whoever relies upon God - then He is sufficient for him

. The meaning of that is: God will accomplish His purpose in every situation, whether the servant relies upon Him or not. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha:
m: h
And whoever relies upon God - then He is sufficient for him
. Indeed, God will accomplish His purpose.” Whether he relies upon Him or not, the one who relies upon Him will have his sins forgiven and will receive a great reward.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq,
m: something similar.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Salt told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: h
And whoever relies upon God - then He is sufficient for him

. He said: He is not someone who relies upon God whose need has been met, and He has made the superiority of the one who relies upon Him over the one who does not relied upon Him, that He will forgive his sins and increase his reward. He said: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: Shatir bin Shakl and Masruq sat together, and Shatir said: Either you narrate what you heard from Ibn Mas’ud and I will believe you, or I will narrate it and you will believe me. Masruq said: No, narrate it and I will believe you. He said: I heard Ibn Mas’ud say: The greatest verse in the Qur’an in terms of delegation is:
h
And whoever relies upon God - then He is sufficient for him
. Masruq said: You have spoken the truth. And His statement,
h
God has set a measure for everything

, means that God Almighty says: God has set a limit, a term, and a measure for everything, including divorce, waiting period, and other things, to which it must end. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq:
m: h
God has set a measure for everything
. He said: A term.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq,
m: h
God has set a measure for everything
. He said: The end.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
God has set a [decreed] extent for everything
, he said: Menstruation in the term and waiting period.

x: God Almighty says: And women who have ceased to desire menstruation, so let them not expect to menstruate from your women if you have any doubt.
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of his statement,
, so some of them said: The meaning of that is:
about the blood that appears from her due to her old age, whether it is menstruation or istihadah, then their waiting period is three months.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
If you are in doubt
, if you do not know the one who stopped menstruating and the one who did not menstruate, then their waiting period is three months.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri,
m: h
If you are in doubt

- he said: Regarding her old age, that is, in her old age, then when she is in doubt, she observes a waiting period of three months. But if a woman’s menstruation stops while she is young, then she should wait until it is determined whether she is pregnant or not. If her pregnancy is clear, then her waiting period is until she gives birth. If her pregnancy is not clear, then until it is clear, and the maximum of that is one year.

c: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation
h
if you are in doubt

, their waiting period is three months, he said: If she is in doubt that she does not menstruate and her menstruation has stopped, or the men are in doubt, or she says: My menstruation has left me, then their waiting period is three months if there is doubt. So if the pregnancy is present, then one should wait until nine months have passed, and he and she are afraid and doubt that menstruation has stopped, then a Muslim woman should not be detained, so she should observe her waiting period of three months. And God, may He be glorified and praised, has also made the waiting period for the young girl who has not menstruated three months.

c: Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma’bad informed us, saying:
m: Sulayman was asked about the woman who is in doubt. He said: She is the woman who is in doubt and has stopped having children. She is divorced, and she menstruates once. Then the time for her second menstrual period comes and she does not menstruate. He said: She observes a waiting period when she is in doubt for three months to come. He said: If she menstruates twice and the time for the third period comes and she does not menstruate, she observes a waiting period when she is in doubt for three months to come, and she does not observe a waiting period for what has passed.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is:
about their ruling and do not know what the ruling is regarding their waiting period, then their waiting period is three months.

c: Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa’ib told us: Ibn Idris told us: Mutraf told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Salim, who said: Ubayy ibn Ka’b said:
m: O Messenger of God, a number of women were not mentioned in the Book, whether they were young or old, or pregnant. So God revealed: “
h
And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation
h
if you are in doubt
, their period is three months. And for those who have not menstruated,
h
and for those who are pregnant
, their term is until they give birth.”

x: Others said: The meaning of this is:
about the blood that appears from them, and you do not know whether it is menstrual blood or istihadha blood due to old age or an illness.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-A’la told us: Sa’id told us,
m: on Surat al-Talaq 65:4
h
And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation

, if you doubt, their waiting period is three months. And for those who have not menstruated and those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth. And whoever fears God - He will make for him of his matter ease. the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Among the doubtful matters is the woman who suffers from istihadah, and whose menstruation is not regular, she menstruates several times a month, and once in a few months, so her waiting period is three months, and this is the opinion of Qatada. The first of the sayings that is correct is the saying of the one who said: What is meant by that is:
h
If you are in doubt
and do not know what the ruling is regarding them. That is because if the meaning of that was as it was said by the one who said:
h
If you are in doubt

about their blood and do not know whether it is menstruation or istihadah, it would have been said: If they are in doubt, because if the blood is unclear to them, then they are the ones who are in doubt about their own blood, not others. And in His saying:
h
If you are in doubt and His addressing men with that and not women is clear evidence of the correctness of what we said
, that its meaning is:
h
If you are in doubt
, O men, about the ruling regarding them. And another is that He, may His praise be glorified, said:
h
And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation
h
if you are in doubt

. And the one who has despaired of menstruation is the one who does not hope for menstruation due to old age. It is impossible to say: And those who have despaired, then to say: You are in doubt about their despair, because despair is the cessation of hope, and the one who is in doubt about her despair has hope for her, and it is not permissible for hope to be lifted and exist at the same time. So if the correct saying about that is what we said, then it is clear that Interpretation of the verse:
h
And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation
h
if you are in doubt

about the ruling concerning them, or their number, and you do not know what they are, then the ruling concerning their number is if they are divorced, and they are among those whose husbands have consummated the marriage, then their waiting period is three months. And those who have not menstruated He says: And likewise the number of those who have not menstruated among the young slave girls if their husbands divorce them after consummation. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation
, he said: Those whose menstruation has stopped, so their waiting period is three months. And those who have not menstruated, he said: The female slaves.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation
, meaning those who have stopped menstruating and do not menstruate, and those who have not menstruated are the virgins who have not menstruated, so their waiting period is three months.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And those who have despaired of menstruation… the verse, he said: The women who have passed the age of menstruation. And those who have not menstruated: They have not reached the age of menstruation, but have touched the earth. Their waiting period is three. His statement,
h
And for those who are pregnant

, their term is until they give birth, regarding the expiration of their waiting period until they give birth, and this is the consensus of all scholars regarding the divorced pregnant woman. As for the woman whose husband has died, there is a difference of opinion among scholars regarding this. We have mentioned their differences in the previous part of this book, and we will mention in this place some of what we did not mention there.

x: Mention of those who said that the ruling on his saying,
And for those who are pregnant
, their term is until they give birth, is general for divorced women and those whose husbands have died.

c: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abaan Al-Masry narrated to us, saying: Saeed bin Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Muhammad bin Jaafar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Shabramah Al-Kufi narrated to me, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Qais, that Ibn Masoud said:
m: Whoever wants, I may curse him. The verse,
h
And for those who are pregnant

, their term is until they give birth was not revealed until after the verse about the woman whose husband has died. And if the woman whose husband has died gives birth, then she is permissible. He meant by the verse about the woman whose husband has died, And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Malik told us,
m: meaning Ibn Ismail, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ibn Atiyyah, who said: I heard Ibn Masoud say: Whoever wants to share it with me, the short Surah An-Nisa was revealed after it, meaning after four months and ten days.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Ayyub told us, on the authority of Muhammad:
m: I met Abu Atiyyah Malik ibn Amir, and I asked him about that, meaning about a woman whose husband has died and who gives birth before the four months and ten days have passed. He started telling me the hadith of Subai’ah. I said: No, have you heard anything from Abdullah about that? He said: Yes, it was mentioned one day or one night in the presence of Abdullah, and he said: Tell me, if the four months and ten days have passed and she has not given birth, is it permissible for her to marry? They said: No. He said: Do you impose strict measures on her and do not give her a dispensation? By God, the short women were revealed after the tall ones.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, he said: Al-Sha’bi said:
m: Whoever wants, I will make an oath to him to reveal the shortened women after the four months and ten that are in Surat Al-Baqarah.

c: Ahmad bin Mani’ told me, he said: Muhammad bin Ubaid told us, he said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: Abdullah bin Mas’ud mentioned the last of the two terms, and he said: Whoever wants, I swear to God that this verse that was revealed about short-term women was revealed after the four months. Then he said: The term for a pregnant woman is until she gives birth to what is in her womb.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, who said:
m: I said to Al-Sha’bi: I do not believe that Ali, may God be pleased with him, used to say: The last of the two terms is that a woman whose husband has died should not marry until the last of the two terms has passed. Al-Sha’bi said: Yes, and he spoke the truth more than I have ever believed anything. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: His statement,
h
And for those who are pregnant

, their term is until they give birth refers to divorced women. Then he said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, and Abdullah used to say about divorce that her term comes to an end when she gives birth. Abu Kurayb narrated: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, who said: When this verse was revealed,
h
And for those who are pregnant
, their term is until they give birth, he said: I said: O Messenger of God, what about the woman whose husband has died and the divorced woman? He said: Yes.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Malik bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Abd al-Karim bin Abi al-Mukhariq, on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b, who said:
m: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about For those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth. He said: The term of every pregnant woman is until she gives birth to what is in her womb.

c: Muhammad told me, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And for those who are pregnant
, their term is until they give birth, he said: The term of every pregnant woman is until she gives birth to what is in her womb.

c: Muhammad told me, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And for those who are pregnant
, their term is until they give birth. He said: For a pregnant woman whose husband divorces her while she is pregnant, her waiting period is until she gives birth.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And for those who are pregnant
, their term is until they give birth. So when she gives birth to what is in her womb, her waiting period has ended. Menstruation has nothing to do with her if she is pregnant.

x: Others said: This is specific to divorced women. As for the woman whose husband has died, her waiting period is the last of the two periods. This is a statement narrated on the authority of Ali and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. We have mentioned the narration of this from them previously. The correct statement about this is that it is general for divorced women and those whose mothers have died, because God, the Exalted, said this in general terms, saying:
And for those who are pregnant

, their term is until they give birth. He did not specify the report about a divorced woman without a deceased woman, rather he made the report general for all pregnant women. If he thought that his statement
And for those who are pregnant

, their term is until they give birth is in the context of report about the rulings on divorced women, not those whose mothers have died, then by telling the ruling on a divorced woman, it is more deserving of being told about them and about those whose mothers have died, because the matter is contrary to what he thought.

That is because, even though it is in the context of report about the rulings on divorced women, it is separate from the report about the rulings on divorced women. Rather, it is report that begins with the rulings on the number of all pregnant women, divorced and non-divorced, and there is no indication that it is intended for some pregnant women and not some of the report of reason, so it is general for what we have explained. And His statement, And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out. God, the Most High, says: And whoever fears God and is in awe of Him, and avoids His disobedience, and performs His obligations, and does not disobey His permission in divorcing his wife, then God will make that divorce easy for him, which is that He will make it easy for him, if he wants to take her back, as long as she is in her waiting period. And if her waiting period ends and then his soul calls him to her, he is able to propose to her.

God Almighty says: This which I have explained to you regarding the ruling on divorce, taking back a wife, and waiting period, is the command of God that He has commanded you with. He has revealed it to you, O people, so that you may obey it and act upon it. And His statement, And whoever fears God - He will remove from him his misdeeds, means: And whoever fears God and fears Him by avoiding His sins and performing His obligations, God will erase his sins and the misdeeds of his deeds. And will make his reward great, means: And He will give him a generous reward for his work and piety. And part of His giving him a generous reward for it is that He will admit him into His Paradise and make him dwell therein forever.

God Almighty says: Lodge your divorced women from the place where you live, “from your means: He says: from the means that you find, and men were only commanded to give them a place to live in from what they find, until they complete their number. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me:
m: He said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement,
h
Lodge them where you dwell
, according to your means, meaning: according to your means.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Whoever finds you, he said: Your means.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Lodge them where you dwell
, according to your means, he said: according to your means.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us,
m: his statement,
h
Lodge them where you dwell
, according to your means,
h
and do not harm them in order to make things difficult for them
, if you cannot find anything except a corner of your house, then let her live there.

c: Muhammad told us: Ahmad told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Lodge them where you dwell
, according to your means, he said: If he divorces a woman, he must provide for her and spend on her.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: I asked him about the words of God Almighty:
h
Lodge them where you dwell

, according to your means. He said: According to your means, wherever you are able. If you cannot find anything, and you are in a dwelling that is not yours, and something comes that takes you out of the dwelling, and you do not have a dwelling to live in, and you cannot find anything, then that is fine. But if he is able to pay rent, then that is his means. He should not evict her from her home. But if he cannot find anything and the owner of the dwelling says: I will not let this woman stay in my house, then no. But if he can find anything, then that is his responsibility. And His statement:
h
And do not harm them in order to make things difficult for them

means, the Most High says: And do not harm them in the dwelling in which you live, and you find spacious houses, so that you do not seek to make things difficult for them. So His statement in order to make things difficult for them means: in order to make things difficult for them in the dwelling even though you have spacious houses. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And do not harm them in order to make things difficult for them
. He said: In housing.

c: Muhammad told me, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement, From your possession, he said: From your power. In His statement:
h
And do not harm them in order to make things difficult for them
, He said: In order to make their dwellings difficult for them until they leave.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan:
m: h
And do not harm them in order to make things difficult for them

. He said: He should not harm her or make her stay difficult for him. Until they give birth. This applies to those who have the right to take her back and to those who do not have the right to take her back. And His statement,
h
And if they are pregnant

, then spend on them until they give birth. God Almighty says: And if your divorced women are pregnant and have become irrevocably divorced from you, then spend on them during their waiting period from you until they give birth. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And if they are pregnant

, then spend on them until they give birth, this is a woman whose husband divorces her, and he announces the divorce while she is pregnant, so God commands him to house her and spend on her until she gives birth, and if she breastfeeds, then until she is weaned. If he announces the divorce and she is not pregnant, then she is entitled to housing until her waiting period is over and there is no maintenance. Likewise, a woman whose husband dies, if she is pregnant, he spends on her from the share of her offspring if there is an inheritance, and if there is no inheritance, then the heir spends on her until she gives birth and weans her child, as God the Almighty said, And upon the heir is the same (al-Baqarah 2:233). If she is not pregnant, then her maintenance is from her own money.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And if they are pregnant
, then spend on them until they give birth, he said: Spending is spent on the pregnant woman if she is pregnant until she gives birth.

x: Others said: What is meant by his saying,
, then spend on them until they give birth is every divorced woman whose husband has the right to take her back or not.
Among those who said this are: Omar bin Al-Khattab and Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with them.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: ‘Umar and Abdullah used to give the divorced woman three rights: housing, maintenance, and compensation. And whenever the hadith of Fatimah bint Qais was mentioned to Umar, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered her to observe her waiting period in a house other than her husband’s, he would say: We would not accept the testimony of a woman in our religion.

c: Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi told me, he said: Yahya bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Isa bin Qurtas, he said:
m: I heard Ali bin Al-Hussein say about the belt three things: she has the right to housing, maintenance, and enjoyment. If she leaves her house, then she has no right to housing, maintenance, or enjoyment.

c: Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: A woman who has been divorced three times is entitled to housing and maintenance.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: If a man divorces her three times, she is entitled to housing and maintenance. The correct statement in this regard, in our view, is that there is no maintenance for a woman whose divorce has been irrevocably interrupted unless she is pregnant, because God, the Most High, made maintenance, in His saying,
h
And if they are pregnant

, then spend on them, for pregnant women and not for others who have been irrevocably divorced. If those who have been irrevocably divorced were the same as those who are pregnant and not pregnant in their obligation to spend on their husbands, there would be no clear reason for mentioning pregnant women specifically in this context, since they and others are the same in this regard, and mentioning them specifically and not for others is the most conclusive evidence that there is no maintenance for a woman who has been irrevocably divorced unless she is pregnant. And with what we said about that, the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is correct.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hakam told me: Bishr ibn Bakr told us, on the authority of al-Awza’i: Yahya ibn Abi Katheer told us: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman told me:
m: Fatimah bint Qays, the sister of al-Dahhak ibn Qays, told me that Abu Amr al-Mahzumi divorced her three times and ordered that she be given maintenance, but she did not like it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent him to Yemen. Khalid ibn al-Walid went with a group of Banu Makhzum to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was with Maymunah. He said: O Messenger of God, Abu Amr divorced Fatimah three times. Is she entitled to maintenance? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: She is not entitled to maintenance. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent word to her: Move to the house of Umm Sharik, and he sent word to her: Do not get ahead of me. Then he sent word to her: The first emigrants will come to Umm Sharik, so move to Ibn Umm Maktum, and if you remove your veil, he will not see you. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her to Usamah ibn Zayd. And His saying:
h
If they breastfeed for you

, then give them their payment. God Almighty says: If your women who are divorced among you breastfeed for you their children, your young ones, for payment, then give them their payment for breastfeeding them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that? Surat Al-Alaq: 14 Does he not know that God sees?

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, that he said
m: about breastfeeding: If he is responsible for something, then the mother of the child has more right to it. If she wishes, she may breastfeed him, and if she wishes, she may leave him, unless he does not accept it from anyone else. If that is the case, she is forced to breastfeed him.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
If they breastfeed for you
, then give them their compensation, she has more right to her child than to take it in exchange for you breastfeeding someone else.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
If they breastfeed for you
, then give them their due compensation. He said: What they agreed upon the wealthy according to his ability, and the poor according to his ability.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding a boy who is paid a price, his mother has more right to breastfeed him. If he cannot find anyone to breastfeed him, the mother is forced to breastfeed him. He said: Thabit Mahran, on the authority of Sufyan, Give them their wages. He said: If she breastfeeds him for a wage, then she is more deserving of it than anyone else. But if she refuses to breastfeed him and does not agree to what is between you and her, then she will be difficult for you to pay, so have another breastfeed him for him. And His statement,
h
And consult one another in what is right

, God Almighty says: And let some of you, O people, accept from others what some of you have commanded others to do of right. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And consult one another in what is right
, he said: Do what is right among yourselves.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan:
m: h
And consult one another in what is right
, urging some of them to do good to others. And His statement:
h
And if you disagree

, then another woman shall breastfeed him. He says: If the man and woman disagree about breastfeeding her child from him, and she refuses to breastfeed him, then he has no right over her, and he does not have the right to force her to breastfeed him, but he should hire a wet nurse for the boy other than his mother who is divorced from him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And if you disagree

, another woman shall nurse him, he said: If the mother refuses to nurse her child if his father divorces her, another wet nurse should be sought for him. The mother is more deserving if she is satisfied with the reward for nursing what someone else is satisfied with, so it should not be taken away from her.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, who said:
m: If she refuses to breastfeed him and does not agree to the terms between her and you, she will be difficult for you to pay, so ask another woman to breastfeed him.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about the statement of God, “
h
And if you disagree

, another woman shall nurse him. Let one with an abundance spend from his abundance, and he whose provision is restricted - let him spend from what God has given him.” He said: He imposed on her from what he could find, so she said: I am not satisfied with this. He said: This is after separation, but as she is his wife, she will nurse him willingly or unwillingly, whether she wants to or refuses. So he said to her: I have nothing more than this. If you like to nurse this woman, then nurse her, and if you do not want to, then let my son be nursed. So this is His statement,
h
And if you disagree
, another woman shall nurse him.

x: Let the one with an abundance spend from his abundance

, and he whose provision is restricted - let him spend from what God has given him means: God Almighty says: Let the one whose wife has separated from him, if he has an abundance of money and is rich, spend from his abundance of money and riches on his divorced wife as a reward for breastfeeding his child from her, and on his young child. And he whose provision is restricted means: And he whose provision is restricted and is not made easy for him, let him spend from what God has given him according to the extent of his money and what he was given from it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
Let the one with an abundance spend from his abundance
. He said: From the abundance of his wealth. He said: And he whose provision is restricted. He said: He whose provision is scarce.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan:
m: Let the one with wealth spend from his wealth, meaning: from his capacity.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Let the one with an abundance spend from his abundance
, and he whose provision is restricted - let him spend from what God has given him, he said: He imposed on her from what he could find.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Let the one with wealth spend from his wealth, he said: on the divorced woman if she breastfeeds him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, who said:
m: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, was asked about Abu Ubaidah, and it was said to him: He wears coarse clothes and eats the coarseest food. So he sent him a thousand dinars and said to the messenger: See what he will do when he takes them. It was not long before he wore the softest clothes and ate the best food.

c: Then the messenger came and informed him,
m: and he, may God have mercy on him, said: Interpret this verse: Let one with an abundance spend from his abundance, and he whose provision is restricted - let him spend from what God has given him. And His statement:
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity

, meaning: God does not charge anyone with the expenses of those he is obligated to pay by blood or kinship except what He has given him. If he is wealthy, then it is from his wealth, and if his provision is restricted, then it is from what God has provided him according to his ability. He does not charge the poor person with the expenses of the wealthy, nor does He charge anyone of His creation except what He has imposed upon him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity
, he said: He says: The poor person is not charged the same as the rich person.

c: Abdullah bin Muhammad Al-Zuhri told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisham:
m: h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity
. He said: Except what He has imposed upon it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan:
m: h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity
. He said: Except what it can bear.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity

, he said: God does not charge him to give charity when he does not have anything to give charity with, nor does God charge him to pay zakat when he does not have anything to pay zakat with. God Almighty says: God will grant to the one who has limited money, after hardship, ease. He says: after hardship, ease, after narrowness, spaciousness, and after poverty, wealth. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan:
m: God will bring about ease after hardship, meaning after hardship comes ease.

x: And how many a town has rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers

. God Almighty says: And how many a town’s people have rebelled against the command of their Lord and disobeyed Him and the command of the messengers of their Lord, so they persisted in their rebellion and insolence, and persisted in their disbelief. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us: Asbat told us on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And how many a city has rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers
, he said: It has changed and disobeyed.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And how many a town disobeyed the command of its Lord and His messengers

, so We brought it to a severe account, he said: Disobedience here means disbelief and disobedience. Disobedience means disbelief. Disobeyed the command of its Lord means it abandoned it and did not accept it. It was said that they were a people who disobeyed the command of their Lord regarding divorce, so God threatened this nation with the report about them that He would do to them what He did to them if they disobeyed His command in that.

c: Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me, saying: Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, saying:
m: I heard Umar ibn Sulayman say regarding His statement,
h
And how many a town has rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers
, he said: A town that was punished for divorce. His statement,
h
So We held her to a severe account
, means:
h
